title: Advertise the IRCv3 capabilities mimid can honour
description:
The capabilities mimid does not advertise, which is where a verb becomes reachable. A client sends what CAP LS offered and nothing else, so the verbs of bead mimid-1wgh.140.5 are unreachable without this, and several client behaviours mimid already supports go unused.

ADVERTISED TODAY (crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/register.rs): batch, draft/chathistory, draft/event-playback, draft/message-redaction, draft/read-marker, echo-message, message-tags, multi-prefix, sasl, server-time, soju.im/account-required, soju.im/webpush.

WORTH ADDING, each specified in ~/PROJECT/IETF/specs as ircv3-<name>.md:

- away-notify: tells a client when a user's away state changes. mimid already answers AWAY, so the state exists and nothing propagates it.
- extended-join, account-notify, account-tag: carry the account a nick belongs to. A nick is not an identity here and the user URI is the thing that matters, so these are the standard way to show a client which MIMI user a nick is, rather than hoping the nick is enough. This is the same problem WHOWAS addresses after the fact (bead mimid-1wgh.140.3).
- invite-notify: makes an invite visible to a channel's members rather than only to the invited user.
- labeled-response: pairs a reply with the command that caused it. Worth more here than on a network, because a mimid reply can be slow: a sync or a Commit stands between the command and its answer, which is the whole subject of bead mimid-604m.
- utf8only: mimid is UTF-8 throughout and its casemapping is its own; advertising it states a fact rather than adding behaviour.
- standard-replies: the front end already sends FAIL, so this is advertising what it does.
- chghost: marginal, listed for completeness, since a mimid nick's host does not change.

FOR EACH ONE: read its spec file before writing anything, implement what it requires rather than the name, and add it to CAP LS and to docs/design/agent-frontends.md with the file it came from. A capability advertised and not honoured is worse than one absent, because a client then changes its behaviour on a promise.

NOT A CAPABILITY LIST FOR ITS OWN SAKE: anything here that mimid cannot honour completely stays unadvertised, and the bead's close reason says which were left out and why.
close_reason:
Three offered, in commit 2f7d2ed0 (branch irc-verbs): extended-join and
account-tag, which carry the MIMI user URI a nick stands for, and
standard-replies, the FAIL format the front end already wrote for
CHATHISTORY, METADATA, REDACT, MONITOR and ACCOUNT_REQUIRED. The account
tag goes to a client that asked for account-tag whether or not it also
asked for message-tags, which ircv3-message-tags.md "Capabilities" makes
a MUST and HexChat's capability set needs. A line that is not UTF-8 is
answered FAIL * INVALID_UTF8 to a client with standard-replies, and the
NOTICE stays for the others.

Left out, each because no line exists to send it, not for want of work:
away-notify (no away state anywhere: AWAY answers 305 and 306 and stores
nothing, WHO's flags are always H or H@, and §4 already says there is no
301 because MIMI carries no presence); account-notify (a nick's account
is its user URI and is never moved to another person, so ACCOUNT could
never be sent); invite-notify (the participant record names no inviter,
so a remote member's add cannot be told from a join); chghost (the user
and host are the URI's local part and domain and neither changes);
labeled-response (the echo of a PRIVMSG, the JOIN of a JOIN and the
TOPIC of a TOPIC come back from the change feed and not from the
command's dispatch, so the label would have to be carried through the
outbox and the feed; docs/irc-lessons.md says to offer it only when
every reply carries the label).

utf8only is not a capability: ircv3-utf8-only.md defines an ISUPPORT
token, which 005 has sent since v1. What that document gives is the
INVALID_UTF8 reply code, which a server publishing UTF8ONLY may send
whether or not any capability was negotiated.

The bead's premise, that bead mimid-1wgh.140.5's verbs are unreachable
without this, is answered rather than met: MONITOR announces itself
through the 005 token alone, and the setname and extended-monitor
capabilities must never be offered, since mimid refuses SETNAME. Neither
verb waits on a capability.

Two beads came out of it: decision mimid-1wgh.150 (the account of a nick
that cannot be written on the wire, closed) and mimid-1wgh.140.11 (an
Identity minted from a user URI must be writable on the wire, which 330,
311, 352 and every hostmask need as much as these two capabilities do,
with the NICK :foo bar parse found while reading).

Also here, both touching lines this bead writes: Out::to_wire now writes
the server's tags before the client-only ones, which
ircv3-message-tags.md makes a MUST, and a client with server-time and no
message-tags now gets the time tag, which the per-tag gate fixed with
the account one.

Gates: cargo fmt --all --check, typos, cargo clippy --workspace
--all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings, RUSTDOCFLAGS doc build,
cargo test -p mimid-agent-irc --all-features (44), and mimid-agent's
irc_v2, irc, irc_two_providers, front_end_auth, no_token_in_logs, rehash
and tailnet suites. The rest of mimid-agent's suites could not be linked:
the machine's disk is full (440M free of 907G), which stops the linker
and not the code.
